cues.en: I'm going to ask you, I'm going to ask you three multiple choice questions. Use this device, use this device to answer. The first question is how did the number of deaths per year from natural disaster, how does that change during the last century? Did it more than double?
cues.zh: 我要问大家，我要问大家三道选择题。请用这个设备，用这个设备来答题。第一题是：在过去的一个世纪里，每年因自然灾害死亡的人数发生了怎样的变化？是增加了一倍以上吗？

cues.en: Did it remain about the same in the world as a whole, or did it decrease to less than a half? Please answer. Please answer. A, B, or C. I see lots of answers. This is much faster than I do it at universities. They are so slow. They keep thinking, thinking, thinking. Oh, very, very good. And we go to the next question. So how long did women 30 years old in the world go to school? Seven years, five years, or three years? A, B, or C? Please answer. And we go to the next question.
cues.zh: 全球总人数是基本保持不变，还是减少到了一半以下？请作答。请作答。选 A、B 还是 C。我看到很多答案了。这比我在大学里搞得快多了。他们太慢了。一直在想，在想，在想。噢，非常，非常棒。我们来看下一题。全球 30 岁的女性平均上过多少年学？七年、五年，还是三年？A、B 还是 C？请作答。我们来看下一题。

cues.en: In the last 20 years, how did the percentage of people in the world who live in extreme poverty change? Extreme poverty not having enough food for the day. Did it almost double? Did it remain more or less the same, or did it half? A, B, or C? Now, answers. You see, death from national disasters in the world. You can see it from this graph here, from 1900 to 2000. In 1900, there was about...
cues.zh: 在过去的20年里，全球极端贫困人口的比例发生了怎样的变化？极端贫困是指连一天的温饱都无法解决。是几乎翻倍了？是基本保持不变，还是减半了？A、B，还是C？现在来看答案。大家看，这是全球因自然灾害死亡的人数。你可以从这张图表上看到，从1900年到2000年。在1900年，大约有……

cues.en: half a million people who died every year from national disaster, floods, earthquake, volcanic eruption, whatever, you know, droughts. And then, how did that change? We asked, Gapminder asked the public in Sweden. This is how they answered. The Swedish public answered like this. 50% thought it had doubled, 38% said it's more or less the same, 12 said it had halved. This is the best data from the disaster researchers.
cues.zh: 每年大约有50万人死于自然灾害，洪水、地震、火山爆发，或者干旱等等。那么，后来情况如何变化呢？我们，Gapminder调查了瑞典公众。这就是他们的回答。瑞典公众是这样回答的：50%的人认为翻倍了，38%的人认为基本持平，12%的人认为减半了。而这是灾害研究人员给出的最权威数据。

cues.en: It goes up and down and it goes to the Second World War and after that it starts to fall and it keeps falling and it's down to much less than half. The world has been much, much more capable as the decades go back to protect people from this, you know. Only 12% of the Swedes know this. So I went to the zoo and I asked the shimps. The shimps doesn't watch the evening news.
cues.zh: 它起起伏伏，一直持续到二战，之后便开始下降，并持续走低，现在已经降到了不到原来的一半。几十年来，全世界保护人们免受此类灾害的能力已经大大增强了。但只有12%的瑞典人知道这一点。于是我去了动物园，去问了黑猩猩。黑猩猩可不看晚间新闻。

cues.en: So the shimps, you know, they just choose by random. So the Swedes answer worse than random. Now, how did you do? That's you. You were beaten by the shimps, but it was close. You were three times better than the Swedes, you know, but that's not enough. You shouldn't compare yourself to Swedes, you know. You must have higher ambitions in the world. Let's look at the next answer here. Women in school. Here...
cues.zh: 所以你看，黑猩猩只是随机乱选。但瑞典人的答题表现比随机瞎蒙还要差。那么，大家答得怎么样呢？这就是你们的成绩。你们输给了黑猩猩，不过差距很小。你们的表现比瑞典人强三倍，但光这样还不够。你们可不能拿自己跟瑞典人比。在世界上你们得有更高的追求。我们来看下一个答案，女性受教育情况。在这里……

cues.en: You can see men went eight years. How long did women go to school? Well, we ask the Swedes like this. And that gives you a hint, doesn't it? The right answer is probably the one where few Swedes pick, isn't it? Let's see. Let's see. Here we come. Yes, yes, yes. Women have almost catched up. This is the US public. This is the US public. And this is you. Here you come.
cues.zh: 大家可以看到男性受教育年限是8年。那女性上学多久呢？我们是这样问瑞典人的。这其实给你们提了个醒，对吧？正确答案很可能是很少有瑞典人选的那个，不是吗？我们来看看。看看结果。来了。是的，没错。女性已经几乎赶上来了。这是美国公众的答案。这是美国公众的。而这是你们的答案。你们的结果出来了。

cues.en: Why, congratulations, you're twice as good at the Swedes, but you're not with me. So, how come? I think it's like this that everyone is aware of that there are countries and there are areas where girls have great difficulties. They are stopped when they go to school, you know. And it's disgusting. But in the majority of the world, where most people in the world live, most countries, girls today go to school as long as boys, more or less.
cues.zh: 哎呀，恭喜，你们的表现是瑞典人的两倍好，但你们还是没能跟上我。那么，为什么会这样呢？我认为情况是这样的：大家都知道有些国家和地区，女童上学面临着巨大的困难。她们在上学路上被阻拦，你们懂的。这令人作呕。但在世界上大多数地方，在绝大多数人生活的大多数国家，如今女童的受教育年限基本上和男童一样长了。

cues.en: That doesn't mean that gender equity is achieved, not at all. They still are confronted to terrible, terrible limitations, but schooling is there in the world today. Now, we miss the majority. When you answer, you answer according to the worst places, and there you are right, but you miss the majority. What about poverty? Well, it's very clear that poverty here was almost halved.
cues.zh: 这并不意味着已经实现了性别平等，完全没有。她们依然面临着极其严峻的限制，但当今世界确实已经普及了基础教育。然而，我们忽略了大多数人。大家回答时，总是依据最糟糕的地方来答，从这方面看你们是对的，但你们却忽略了大多数人。那贫困问题呢？很显然，这里的贫困率几乎减半了。

cues.en: And in the US, when we asked the public, only 5% got it right. And you? Ah, you almost made it to the shimp. There must be preconceived ideas, you know. And many in the rich countries, they think that, oh, we can never end extreme poverty. Of course they think so, because they don't even know what has happened.
cues.zh: 在美国，我们调查公众时，只有5%的人答对了。那你们呢？哈，你们答得差点就赶上黑猩猩了。这肯定是有先入为主的成见在作怪。富裕国家的很多人都觉得，哎呀，我们永远不可能消除极端贫困。他们当然会这么想，因为他们甚至都不知道已经发生了什么。

cues.en: The first thing to think about the future is to know about the present. These questions were a few of the first ones in the pilot phase of the Ignorance Project in Gapminder Foundation that we run. And it was started this project last year by my boss and also my son, Ola Rosling, his co-founder and director. And he wanted, Ola told me we had to be more systematic when we fight devastating ignorance.
cues.zh: 思考未来的第一步，是了解当下。这些问题只是我们运营的 Gapminder Foundation 在开展“无知项目”（Ignorance Project）试点阶段时提出的前几个问题。该项目是去年由我的老板兼儿子 Ola Rosling 发起的，他是联合创始人兼负责人。他希望，Ola 告诉我，我们在对抗这种破坏性的无知时，必须更加系统化。

cues.en: So already the pilots revealed this, that so many in the public score were worse than random. So we had to think about preconceived ideas. And one of the main preconceived ideas is about world income distribution. Look here, this is how it was 1975. It's the number of people on each income. From one dollar, one dollar a day. See, there was one hump here, around one dollar a day.
cues.zh: 初步试验就已经表明，公众得分比随机蒙还要差的人太多了。所以我们得考虑人们的固有观念。其中一个主要的固有观念就是关于全球收入分配的。看这里，这就是1975年的情况。这是各收入水平对应的人口数量。从一美元，每天一美元算起。瞧，这里有个驼峰，大概在每天一美元左右。

cues.en: And then there was one hump here, somewhere between $10 and $100. The world was two groups. It was a camel world, like a camel with two humps. The poor one and the rich ones. And there were fewer in between. But look how this has changed. As I go forward, what has changed, the world population has grown, you know, and the humps start to merge. The lower hump merged with the upper hump. And the camel dies, and we have a dramatura world with one hump only.
cues.zh: 然后这里还有一个驼峰，在10到100美元之间。世界分成了两组。那是一个骆驼型的世界，就像一只双峰驼。穷的一峰和富的一峰。中间的人要少得多。但看看这发生了怎样的变化。随着时间向前推移，变化的是，世界人口增长了，而且这两个峰开始合并。低处的驼峰融入了高处的驼峰。双峰驼消失了，我们迎来了只有单个驼峰的单峰驼世界。

cues.en: The percent in poverty has decreased, still it's appalling that so many remain in extreme poverty. We still have this group, almost a billion over there, but that can be ended now. The challenge we have now, you know, is to get away from the, understand what the majority is, and that is very clearly shown in this question. We asked...
cues.zh: 贫困人口的比例下降了，但仍有这么多人处于极度贫困之中，这依然令人震惊。我们仍有这个群体，那边有近十亿人，但这种情况现在是可以终结的。大家知道，我们现在的挑战在于摆脱误解，看清大多数人的真实状况，而这个问题很清楚地说明了这一点。我们问……

cues.en: What is the percentage of the world's one-year-old children who have got those basic vaccines against measles and other things that we have had for many years? Twenty, fifty or eighty percent. Now, this is what the US public and the Swedish answered. And you say, look at the Swedish result, you know what the right answer is. The heck is Professor of Global Health in that country? Well, it's me. It's me. You see, it's very difficult. It's very difficult. However, Ola's approach
cues.zh: 全世界一岁儿童中，接种了麻疹等多年常规基础疫苗的比例是多少？百分之二十、五十还是八十？这是美国和瑞典公众的回答。你可能会说，看看瑞典的结果，你就知道正确答案是什么了。到底谁是那个国家的全球卫生学教授啊？好吧，就是我。正是在下。你看，这真的很难。真的很难。然而，Ola 这种

cues.en: to really measure what we know, made headlines. And CNN published these results on their web, and they had the questions there, millions answered, and I think there was about 2,000 comments. And this was one of the comments, you know. I bet no member of the media passed the test, he said. So, Ula told me, take these devices, you are invited to media conferences, give it to them, and measure what the media know. And, ladies and gentlemen, for the first time, the informal result,
cues.zh: 真正衡量大家认知的方法引发了轰动。CNN 在其网站上发布了这些结果，并把问题放在上面，数百万人参与了答题，我想大概有两千条评论。其中有这样一条评论。他说，我敢打赌媒体人没有一个能通过这个测试。于是 Ula 对我说，带上这些答题器，你受邀去参加媒体大会时给他们做做，测测媒体人到底知道多少。女士们，先生们，今天首次公布非正式结果，

cues.en: from a conference with US media and then lately from the European Union media. You see, the problem is not that people don't read and listen to the media. The problem is that the media doesn't know themselves. What shall we do about this, Ola? Do you have an idea? Yes, I have an idea. But first, I'm so sorry that you were beaten by the chimps.
cues.zh: 先是参加了一场美国媒体的会议，最近又参加了欧盟媒体的。你看，问题不在于大家不看、不听媒体报道。问题在于媒体自己也不懂。对此我们该怎么办呢，Ola？你有什么主意吗？是的，我有个主意。但首先，很遗憾你们居然被黑猩猩打败了。

cues.en: Fortunately, I will be able to comfort you by showing why it was not your fault, actually. Then I will equip you with some tricks for beating the chimps in the future. That's basically what I will do. But first, let's look at why are we so ignorant. And it all starts in this place. It's Hudiksvall. It's a city in northern Sweden. It's a neighborhood where I grew up. And it's a neighborhood with a large problem.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，我能给你们些安慰，告诉你们这其实不是你们的错。然后我会传授大家一些技巧，好让你们在将来能击败黑猩猩。基本上这就是我要做的事。但首先，让我们来看看为什么我们对此一无所知。而这一切都始于这个地方。这里是胡迪克斯瓦尔。它是瑞典北部的一座城市。这是我长大的社区。也是一个有着大麻烦的社区。

cues.en: Actually, it has exactly the same problem which existed in all the neighborhoods where you grew up as well. It was not representative. OK? It gave me a very biased view of how life is on this planet. So this is the first piece of the ignorance puzzle. We have a personal bias. We have all different experiences from communities and people we meet. And on top of this, we start school and we add the next problem. Well, I like schools, but teachers ...
cues.zh: 其实，它和大家成长环境里的所有社区有着完全相同的问题。它不具备代表性，明白吗？它让我对这个星球上的生活产生了非常片面的看法。这就是构成无知拼图的第一块。我们都带有个人偏见。我们从所处的社区和遇见的人身上，获得了各不相同的经历。在此之上，我们开始上学，又迎来了下一个问题。我很喜欢学校，但老师们……

cues.en: tend to teach outdated world view because they learned something when they went to school and now they describe this word to the students without any bad intentions and those books of course that are printed are outdated in a world that changes.
cues.zh: 往往会传授过时的世界观，因为那是他们当年上学时学到的东西，现在他们毫无恶意地把这个世界描述给学生，当然，在这个瞬息万变的世界里，印出来的那些书本早就过时了。

cues.en: And there is really no practice to keep the teaching material up to date, so that's what we're focusing on. So we have these outdated facts added on top of our personal bias. What happens next is news, okay? An excellent journalist knows how to pick the story that will make headlines, and people will read it because it's sensational. Its unusual events are more interesting. Don't.
cues.zh: 而且确实没有让教材保持更新的惯例，这正是我们目前关注的重点。于是，在个人偏见之上，我们又叠加了这些过时的事实。接下来发生的就是新闻，对吧？优秀的记者懂得如何挑选能上头条的故事，人们也会因为耸人听闻去阅读。不同寻常的事件总是更有趣。别。

cues.en: and they are exaggerated, and especially things we're afraid of would get... I mean, a shark attack on a Swedish person would get headlines for weeks in Sweden, you know? Okay, so these three skewed sources of information was really hard to get away from, wasn't it? You know, they kind of bombardize us and equip our mind with a lot of strange ideas, and on top of it, we put the very thing that makes us humans.
cues.zh: 而且它们被夸大了，尤其是我们害怕的事情会……我是说，如果一个瑞典人遭到鲨鱼袭击，那在瑞典能连上好几周的头条，对吧？好，所以这三种带有偏差的信息来源确实很难摆脱，不是吗？你看，它们就像在轰炸我们，让我们满脑子都是各种奇怪的想法，更重要的是，我们还加上了让人类之所以成为人类的东西。

cues.en: our human intuition. It was good in evolution. It helped us generalize and jump to conclusions very, very fast. It helped us exaggerate what we're afraid of. And we see causality where there is none. And we then get an illusion of confidence where we believe that we are the best car drivers above the average. Everybody answered that question. Yeah, I drive cars better.
cues.zh: 那就是我们人类的直觉。它在进化中曾大有裨益。它帮我们迅速归纳并极快地得出结论。它帮我们放大了我们所恐惧的事物。我们在本无因果的地方生造因果。然后我们就会产生一种自信的错觉，认为自己的驾驶水平高于平均水平。每个人在回答这个问题时都觉得：对啊，我开车水平更好。

cues.en: Okay, this was good evolutionary, but now when it comes to the world view, it is the exact reason why it's upside down. The trends that are increasing are instead falling and the other way around. And in this case, the chimps use our intuition against us, and it becomes our weakness instead of our strength. It was supposed to be our strength, wasn't it? So how do we solve such problems? First, we need to measure it, and then we need to cure it. So by measuring it, we can understand
cues.zh: 好吧，从进化角度看这很合理，但放在对世界的认知上，这恰恰是导致我们认知颠倒的原因。上升的趋势被看作下降，反之亦然。这样一来，大猩猩就利用了我们的直觉，而直觉非但没成为我们的优势，反而成了劣势。它本该是我们的优势，对吧？那我们要怎么解决这类问题呢？首先，我们需要衡量它，然后再去治愈它。通过衡量，我们就能弄清

cues.en: What is the pattern of ignorance? We started the pilot last year and now we're pretty sure that we will encounter a lot of ignorance across the whole world. And the idea is really to scale it up to all domains or dimensions of global development, such as climate, endangered species, human rights, gender equality, energy, finance,
cues.zh: 无知的模式到底是什么？我们去年启动了这个试点项目，现在我们非常确信，全球范围内存在着大量的无知现象。我们的设想是把它推广到全球发展的各个领域或维度，比如气候、濒危物种、人权、性别平等、能源、金融，

cues.en: All different sectors have facts, and there are organizations trying to spread awareness about these facts. So I've started actually contacting some of them, like WWF and Amnesty International and UNICEF, and asking them, what are your favorite facts which you think the public don't know? OK, I gather those facts. Imagine a long list with, say, 250 facts.
cues.zh: 所有不同领域都有事实数据，也都有组织在努力普及这些事实。所以我已经开始联系其中的一些组织，比如 WWF、Amnesty International 和 UNICEF，问他们：“你们最想让公众知道哪些他们其实不了解的事实？”好，我把这些事实收集起来。想象一下，一份列有大概 250 条事实的长清单。

cues.en: And then we poll the public and see where they score worst. So we get a shorter list with the terrible results, like some few examples, Hans, and we had no problems finding these kind of terrible results. This little short list, what are we going to do with it? Well, we turn it into a knowledge certificate, a global knowledge certificate, which you can use if you're a large organization, a school, a university, or maybe a news agency.
cues.zh: 然后我们对公众进行调查，看看他们在哪些方面得分最差。这样我们就得到了一份糟糕结果的简短清单，就像刚才 Hans 举的几个例子一样，我们毫不费力就找到了这些糟糕的结果。这份简短的清单，我们打算拿来做什么呢？好吧，我们把它变成了一份知识认证，一份全球知识认证，如果你是大型机构、学校、大学，或者新闻机构，你都可以使用它。

cues.en: to certify yourself as globally knowledgeable, okay? Basically meaning we don't hire people who score like chimpanzees, you know? Of course you shouldn't. So maybe 10 years from now, if this project succeeds, you will be sitting at an interview having to fill out this crazy global knowledge. So now we come to the practical tricks. How are you going to succeed, okay? There is, of course,
cues.zh: 以此来证明你具备全球认知，好吗？基本上就意味着，我们不招得分还不如黑猩猩的人，对吧？当然不该招。所以也许十年后，如果这个项目成功了，你参加面试时就得填写这份疯狂的全球知识测试。那么现在我们来聊聊实用的小窍门。你该怎么过关呢，对吧？当然有，

cues.en: One way, which is to sit down late nights and learn all the facts by heart, by reading all these reports, that will never happen, actually. Not even Hans thinks that's going to happen. People don't have that time. People like shortcuts. And here are the shortcuts. We need to turn our intuition into strength again. We need to be able to generalize. So now I'm going to show you some tricks where the misconceptions are turned around.
cues.zh: 一种方法，那就是熬夜坐冷板凳，通读所有这些报告，把所有事实硬背下来，但这绝不可能发生。就连 Hans 都不觉得这行得通。人们没有那个时间。大家都喜欢走捷径。捷径就在这里。我们需要让直觉重新成为我们的优势。我们需要学会举一反三。所以现在我要给大家展示一些诀窍，把那些固有偏见给扭转过来。

cues.en: into rules of thumb. Let's start with the first misconception. This is very widely spread. Everything is getting worse. You heard it. You thought it yourself. The other way to think is most things improve. So you're sitting with a question in front of you and you're unsure, you should guess, improve. Don't go for the worse. That will help you score better on our tests. That was the first one.
cues.zh: 变成经验法则。我们先来看第一个误区。这种想法非常普遍：一切都在变得越来越糟。你们听过这种说法，自己也这么想过。另一种思考方式是：大多数事情都在变好。所以当你面对一个拿不准的问题时，你应该猜它变好了。别选变糟的那个。这样能帮你在我们的测试中拿更高的分数。这就是第一个。

cues.en: There are rich and poor, and the gap is increasing. It's a terrible inequality. Yeah, it's an unequal world, but when you look at the data, it's one hump, okay? If you feel unsure, go for the most people are in the middle, okay? That's going to help you get the answer right. Now, the next preconceived idea is first, countries and people need to be very, very rich.
cues.zh: 世界上有富人和穷人，而且贫富差距越来越大。这是一种可怕的不平等。没错，这个世界确实不平等，但你看数据就会发现，它呈现的是单峰分布，明白吗？如果你不确定，就选大多数人处于中等水平，好吗？这能帮你答对题目。那么，下一个固有观念是：国家和人首先必须变得非常、非常富裕。

cues.en: to get the social development like girls in school and be ready for natural disasters. No, no, no, that's wrong. Look, that huge hump in the middle already has girls in school. So if you are unsure, go for the majority already have this, like electricity and girls in school, these kind of things. There are only rules of thumb. Of course they don't apply to everything, but this is how you can generalize. Let's look at the last one. If something ...
cues.zh: 才能实现女童入学等社会发展，并为自然灾害做好准备。不不不，这是错的。看，中间那个巨大的驼峰里，女童已经有学上了。所以如果你拿不准，就选大多数人已经拥有的，比如通电、女童入学这类的。这些只是经验法则。当然它们不适用于所有情况，但你可以这样去概括。我们来看最后一个。如果有什么……

cues.en: Yes, this is a good one. Sharks are dangerous, okay. No, well, yes, but they are not so important in the global statistics. That's what I'm saying. I actually am very afraid of sharks. So as soon as I see a question about things I'm afraid of, which might be earthquakes, other religions, maybe I'm afraid of terrorists or sharks, anything that makes me feel, assume you're going to exaggerate the problem.
cues.zh: 对，这个例子很好。鲨鱼很危险，好吧。不，好吧，确实危险，但在全球统计数据里没那么重要。这就是我想说的。其实我非常怕鲨鱼。所以只要看到关于我害怕的事情的问题，比如地震、其他宗教，或者我害怕恐怖分子或鲨鱼，任何让我有感觉的事物，先假设自己会夸大这个问题。

cues.en: Okay? That's a rule of thumb. Of course, there are dangerous things that are also great. Sharks kill very, very few. That's how you should think. With these four rules of thumb, you could probably answer better than the chimps, because the chimp cannot do this. They cannot generalize these kind of rules. Okay? And hopefully, we can turn your world around, and we're going to beat the chimps. Okay? That's a systematic approach.
cues.zh: 明白了吗？这是一条经验法则。当然，有些危险的事物也同样很棒。鲨鱼杀的人非常非常少。这就是你们应该有的思维方式。有了这四条经验法则，你们的表现大概就能超过黑猩猩了，因为黑猩猩做不到这些。它们无法总结出这类规律。对吧？希望我们能颠覆你的认知，彻底击败黑猩猩。好吗？这就是系统化的方法。

cues.en: Now the question, is this important? Yeah, it's important to understand poverty, extreme poverty, and how to fight it, and how to bring girls in school. When we realize actually it's succeeding, we can understand it. But is it important for everyone else who cares about the rich end of this scale? I would say yes, extremely important for the same reason. If you have a fact-based worldview of today,
cues.zh: 现在的问题是，这重要吗？是的，理解贫困、极度贫困，懂得如何战胜贫困、如何让女孩走进校园，这至关重要。当我们意识到这其实正在取得成功时，我们就能理解它了。但对于其他所有只关心这个尺度上富裕端的人来说，这重要吗？我认为是的，出于同样的原因，它极其重要。如果你对当今世界拥有基于事实的世界观，

cues.en: you might have a chance to understand what's coming next in the future. We're going back to these two humps. In 1975, that's when I was born, and I selected the West. That's the current EU countries and North America. Let's now see how the rest and the West compares in terms of how rich you are. These are the people who can afford to fly abroad with an airplane for a vacation.
cues.zh: 你就更有可能理解未来接踵而至的一切。我们再回到这两个驼峰图。1975年，也就是我出生的那一年，我选出了西方世界。也就是现在的欧盟国家和北美地区。现在让我们看看世界其他地区和西方在财富水平上的对比。这些人是能负担得起坐飞机出国度假的人。

cues.en: In 1975, only 30 percent of them lived outside EU and North America. But this has changed, OK? So first, let's look at the change up till today, 2014. Today, it's 50-50. The Western domination is over, as of today. That's nice. So what's going to happen next? Do you see the big hump? Did you see how it moved?
cues.zh: 1975年，他们当中只有30%生活在欧美以外。但这已经变了，对吧？我们先来看看截至2014年今天的变化。如今，双方各占一半。从今天起，西方的主导地位宣告终结。挺不错的。那么接下来会发生什么？你们看到那个大隆起吗？看到它是怎么移动的了吗？

cues.en: I did a little experiment. I went to the IMF, International Monetary Fund website. They have a forecast for the next five years of GDP per capita. So I can use that to go five years into the future, assuming the income inequality of each country is the same. I did that, but I went even further. I used those five years for the next 20 years with the same speed. Just as an experiment, what might actually happen?
cues.zh: 我做了个小实验。我去了国际货币基金组织（IMF）的网站。他们对未来五年的各国家人均GDP做了预测。假设各国内部收入差距不变，我就可以用这些数据推演未来五年。我照做了，但我还更进一步：我按同样的发展速度，把这五年的趋势推演到了未来20年。纯当是个实验，看看究竟可能会发生什么？

cues.en: Let's move into the future. In 2020, it's 57% in the rest. 2025, 63%, 2030, 68, and in 2035,
cues.zh: 我们放眼未来。到了2020年，其他地区占到57%。2025年是63%，2030年是68%，而到了2035年，

cues.en: the West is outnumbered in the rich consumer market. These are just the projections of GDP per capita into the future. 73% of the rich consumers are going to live outside North America and Europe. So yes, I think it's a good idea for a company to use this certificate to make sure they make fact-based decisions in the future. Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 在富裕消费市场中，西方将被超越。这些只是对未来人均GDP的预测。73%的富裕消费者将生活在北美和欧洲之外。所以没错，我认为企业使用这份认证是个好主意，能确保他们未来做出基于事实的决策。非常感谢。
